text:
Maya: Quick sync — we need a final decision on pilot gating for SLA, pricing tiers, and runbook ownership by EOD today. Customers on the pilot are asking about 95th/99th latency guarantees.
Jon: Can we define separate SLOs for 'interactive' vs 'batch' traffic? Interactive needs p95 latency, batch only throughput.
Priya: Agree. Suggested SLOs: Interactive p95 < 300ms, p99 < 600ms; Batch 99th percentile throughput target 500req/s per dedicated node.
Arjun: Those numbers look tight for some models (long context). We should add conditional SLOs: e.g., seq_len <= 1024 qualifies for those p95/p99; >1024 falls back to best-effort with documented limits.
Liam: We also need to decide how error budget burn ties to rollback policy. My proposal: if p99 latency exceeds target for 3 consecutive 15-min windows OR error rate double baseline for 30m, trigger immediate canary rollback to fallback-quantized model.
Priya: +1 on rollback thresholds. Add: automated alert to #eng-oncall and a ticket created in ops queue with high priority.
Maya: Ops runbook ownership? @Arjun you were volunteering to own the runbook and pager routing for pilot — still good?
Arjun: I can own the runbook. I'll populate step-by-step: detection -> impact assessment -> rollback -> mitigation -> postmortem. Will add contact matrix.
ops-bot: Runbook template created: https://wiki/redwood/runbooks/pilot-sla-template — fill sections "Detection" and "Rollback" before cutover.
Jon: Docs and marketing need a short allowance in release notes: "Latency and cost vary by model and input length; see SLA table." Who will write the customer-facing SLA snippet?
Priya: I'll draft the customer-facing SLA blurbs and the FAQ for pilot customers. Will include explicit examples (tokens, seq_len).
Maya: Pricing readiness — do we ship tiered pricing for pilot or flat trial pricing? Finance wants a simple banded pricing: dev (low volume), pro (production), enterprise (SLA + premium support). We need approximate $/1k tokens or $/req numbers.
Liam: For pilot, let's do a conservative band: dev = $0, pro = base + usage (early-discount), enterprise = committed monthly + reserved capacity uplift. We'll finalize numbers with FinOps tomorrow.
Maya: Ok. Action items: Arjun -> runbook + pager matrix (owner). Priya -> customer SLA blurbs + FAQ. Jon -> coordinate devex snippet + link in docs. Liam -> pricing bands draft for FinOps. I'll take product sign-off.
Priya: Also: monitoring — need explicit dashboards: p95/p99 latency by route, error rate, CPU/GPU utilization, KV cache hit rate, batching efficiency. I'll add a monitoring checklist.
Arjun: Add synthetic probes for the top 10 customer prompt shapes so we catch regressions during rollout.
Maya: Good. Timeline: content + runbook by EOD, pricing draft by COB tomorrow, monitoring probes created before pilot start. If all green, we do a limited 2-week pilot with 3 customers.
Jon: Small note on billing: ensure metering for reserved capacity vs consumed tokens is separated in telemetry. Devex will surface both to customers.
Priya: I'll also include fallback behavior and expected cost delta in the FAQ (e.g., quantized fallback reduces cost ~30% but may affect quality).
Liam: Support readiness: define SLA tiers mapping to oncall escalation — pro = standard, enterprise = priority with direct escalation to SRE lead.
Maya: Perfect. If nobody objects, I'll lock these decisions and update the launch checklist. :thumbsup:
Arjun: No objections, will start filling runbook now.
ops-bot: Reminder: create ticket in #release-war-room when runbook is uploaded.
Maya: Thanks team — I'll post the updated checklist after runbook and docs links are live.
Jon: Thanks, everyone.
